methodology.position_sizing: R-multiple risk-normalized, identical to tools/build_public_metrics.py -- no per-symbol dollar sizing applied.
methodology.transaction_costs: None modeled -- frictionless proxy, identical to tools/build_public_metrics.py.
methodology.no_lookahead: Entries anchored at valid_for (T+1), Mean Reversion entry = Open on valid_for, stop-first exit over the tested horizon -- identical to the corrected methodology in commit 13cb31a, generalized from a hardcoded 5 days to a horizon parameter.
methodology.multiple_comparisons_correction: Bonferroni correction, family_size=12 (3 archetypes x 4 horizons = 12 tests attempted, chosen as the family size even for cells that produce no real p-value, e.g. MOMENTUM at every horizon -- the conservative choice). p_corrected = min(1, p_raw * 12). Bonferroni (family-wise error control) was chosen over Benjamini-Hochberg (false-discovery-rate control) because this investigation's prior expectation is 'probably nothing here' and a false 'found edge' claim is the costlier mistake -- the more conservative control is the appropriate default.

verdict.verdict: no edge ever distinguishable from noise
verdict.reason: 4/17 scored windows (24%) fell outside the random-entry noise band, and the CUSUM change-point test (p=0.0950) did not find a significant break. Apparent ups and downs in the rolling metric are consistent with what a random-entry baseline under the same risk/regime rules would also produce.

Only 5 computable trades in the entire history -- too few for a meaningful rolling-window/change-point analysis (minimum 10 needed for even a single candidate break test). This is itself informative: MOMENTUM has essentially never had enough regime-gated opportunity to generate a testable track record.

overall_verdict.TREND_PULLBACK: No edge distinguishable from noise survives Bonferroni correction at any tested horizon, though the raw (uncorrected) p-value was marginal at 10d (raw p=0.0290) -- exactly the kind of result that would look like a finding without correcting for the 12-test family this sweep runs across.
overall_verdict.MOMENTUM: Insufficient data at every tested horizon (1d=5, 3d=5, 5d=5, 10d=5 trades). Trade count doesn't change with holding-period horizon -- the same signals are just evaluated over a different forward window -- so MOMENTUM's already-thin sample was expected to stay insufficient at every horizon, and it does.
overall_verdict.MEAN_REVERSION: No edge distinguishable from noise at any tested horizon (1d/3d/5d/10d), before or after multiple-comparisons correction. The 'no edge ever distinguishable from noise' verdict from the primary 5-day analysis is robust to holding-period choice, not an artifact of picking 5 days specifically.
